clue.text: Second base rate reduction

parts.note: low-down as an adjective means base, mean or despicable

explanation.surface: A news line about a central bank cutting its base rate for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base rate' reads as one banking term, but 'base' is split off as its own piece and 'rate reduction' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in speed or pace of activity is a reduction in its rate.

clue.text: Spooner's choice for one's remuneration during disorder

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner famously did

parts.note: a pick is a choice
say, like 'for one', introduces an example

explanation.surface: Someone choosing what they will be paid while laid low by illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial sounds of PICK and SAY gives SICK PAY. 'Disorder' here means illness, not chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid by an employer while a worker is off ill, a disorder being an ailment.

clue.text: Show too much faith in patent on corrosion

parts.note: patent as an adjective means open and obvious
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Placing excessive confidence in a patent protecting a process against corrosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like the legal monopoly, but here it is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust excessively is to show more faith than is warranted.

clue.text: The German on dating app briefly is stylish and attractive

parts.note: das is a German word for 'the'

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Hinge is a well-known dating app

explanation.surface: A German man on a dating app comes across as fashionable and good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing describes someone smart, confident and attractive, especially in appearance.

clue.text: Hair in drink, not unknown, right?

indicators.note: not says the unknown is to be left out of the drink

parts.note: whiskey is a drink
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A diner spots a hair in their drink and asks whether that can really be right.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisker is a single hair, especially on the face.

clue.text: Cover article involved in reproduction

indicators.note: involved in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a copy is a reproduction
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A magazine cover story about reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as a fabric awning.

clue.text: President's win following smart cut

indicators.note: following places the win after the clipped word
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: clever means smart
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A president's electoral victory comes after a sharp cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart cut' sounds like a sharp haircut or a deft reduction, but 'cut' trims the R from CLEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was twice President of the United States.

clue.text: Husband interrupts sleep with position where risk is worth taking

definitions.text: position where risk is worth taking

indicators.note: interrupts says the husband breaks into the run of letters

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
and can mean with, as in 'bread and butter'

explanation.surface: A husband disturbs a nap, a risk worth running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interrupts' puts the husband inside the run of two pieces. Nap is a card game in which a nap hand, one likely to win all five tricks, justifies a bold bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap hand is a strong position in which taking a chance is likely to pay off.

clue.text: Philip exposed compiler as sucker for science

parts.note: Pip is a short form of Philip

indicators.note: exposed means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter

explanation.surface: Philip unmasks the puzzle-setter as a gullible science fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like an insult for the setter, but it is part of the definition: a pipette sucks up liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is a laboratory tube that draws up small measured volumes of liquid by suction.

clue.text: Perhaps Queen's musical composition

parts.note: Chess is a stage musical by Benny Andersson, Bjorn Ulvaeus and Tim Rice
a piece is a musical or written composition

explanation.surface: A musical work by the rock band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band given 'musical composition', but it is the chessboard queen, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is one of the pieces used in the board game of chess, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: The most important Catholic is Father Ted, essentially

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or centre of the word Ted

explanation.surface: Father Ted, the comic TV priest, as the leading figure of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is an Irish TV sitcom about a hapless priest; the clue splits 'Father' and 'Ted' into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Roman Catholic Church is its supreme figure.

clue.text: Actor's wife trips attacker up

indicators.note: up here means in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor's wife trips up an assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips ... up' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'up' is the signal to rearrange W, TRIPS and ATTACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Patrick Stewart is an English actor known for Star Trek and the X-Men films.

clue.text: Less experienced guy, one upset by Blackadder's ending

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of Blackadder

explanation.surface: A naive man, one of the characters thrown by the finale of the TV comedy Blackadder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges the two words; Blackadder is a British TV sitcom whose famous final episode the surface evokes, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of fewer years generally means having less experience.

clue.text: Period of celebration once politician in Ireland departs, indeed

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A politician leaves Ireland at a time of festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: Empire Day, 24 May, was celebrated across the British Empire until it was renamed in 1958, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Empire Day was an annual holiday of patriotic celebration, now discontinued.

clue.text: Wanting it more organised, rearranged ride

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, so ran means organised

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters of ride are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone keen for a better-organised ride that had to be rescheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting it' is a coy phrase for sexual desire, which the comparative adjective expresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy means lustful, so the comparative describes someone with greater sexual appetite.

clue.text: Press corps, powerless after reforming, beginning to seek medal

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes

indicators.note: reforming means the remaining letters are formed anew in another order
powerless means the P, standard for power, is removed
beginning to points to the first letter of seek

explanation.surface: The press corps, stripped of power and in reform, starts hunting for honours.
explanation.walkthrough: CORPS without P leaves CORS, rearranged as CROS, then S from 'seek'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Muse, content to neuter pets

indicators.note: content means what is held within these clue words

explanation.surface: A muse of inspiration is happy to see pets neutered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content to' reads as 'willing to', but 'content' means the letters contained in the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe was the Greek Muse of music and lyric poetry.

clue.text: Country drops back to serve another

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom
rain falls in drops

indicators.note: back to points to the final letter of serve

explanation.surface: A country retreats in order to help a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like the definition, but it gives UK; 'another' (another country) defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a further nation following on from the country already named in the clue.

clue.text: Each short rest is most relaxed

indicators.note: short means the word is clipped of its last letter

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon rest

explanation.surface: A brief break taken each time is the most restful.
explanation.definitionFit: The least tense or troublesome is the most free of strain.

clue.text: American study papers over cracks regarding biological tissue

parts.note: a den is a private study

indicators.note: cracks means the letters break apart and re-form

parts.note: ID is identity papers
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An American study that glosses over flaws in research on body tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers over cracks' reads as concealing faults; here 'cracks' breaks ID and O apart to make OID.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoid as an adjective means glandular, relating to lymphatic tissue.

clue.text: Voracious eater with big nose, Anthea Turner finally making husband billions

indicators.note: the H for husband is replaced by B for billions
finally points to the last letter of Turner

explanation.surface: TV presenter Anthea Turner's spouse turns out to be a billionaire with a big appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthea Turner is a British TV presenter. The antbear, or aardvark, eats huge numbers of ants with its long snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark, also called the antbear, has a long snout and devours termites in vast numbers.

clue.text: Protein in fool's beer rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool, with 's giving NITS
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A fool's beer contains protein that makes it froth up.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the elastic connective-tissue protein in skin and blood vessels.

clue.text: Think about fellow eating handsomely

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
well can mean handsomely, as in 'well paid'

explanation.surface: A man eating a generous meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on a subject is to keep thinking about it at length.

clue.text: Funds kept back from park and large farm in outskirts of Tallahassee

parts.note: a reserve is a protected park for wildlife

indicators.note: in puts the farm between the outer letters
outskirts of points to the first and last letters of Tallahassee

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: Money kept aside from a nature park and a big farm on the edge of the Florida capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Tallahassee is the capital of Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve tranche is a portion of funds held back, notably a country's reserve allocation at the IMF.

clue.text: Heartless French girl's put on record

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: fille is French for girl

explanation.surface: A heartbroken French girl has gone on record.
explanation.definitionFit: To file a document is to enter it officially into the records.

clue.text: Leaves fuel in arid ground

parts.note: deserts means leaves or abandons
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Fallen leaves are fuel lying on dry earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a noun for foliage, but it is the verb meaning abandons.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert soil is the dry, sandy earth of an arid region.

clue.text: Extremely arresting stone church's storage room

indicators.note: arresting means catching hold of, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: very means extremely
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A remarkably striking stone church with a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely arresting' reads as 'very striking', but 'arresting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where vestments and sacred items are kept.

clue.text: Introduces tolls to get rid of borders

indicators.note: borders means the disposal word forms the edges round the bells

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
a bell rings when it tolls

explanation.surface: A government brings in tolls in order to scrap border controls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get rid of borders' suggests removing outer letters, but BIN itself borders RINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in a law or practice is to introduce it.
